skill.name: styling-with-shadcn
skill.description: Build accessible shadcn/ui interfaces for Next.js applications. The skill covers setup, component patterns, forms with react-hook-form and Zod, dialogs, tables, sidebars, toasts, and dark mode.
skill.summary: Create polished shadcn/ui interfaces for React and Next.js projects.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, TSX examples, CSS template literals, and documentation text. Three command-related findings are confirmed because the skill tells users to run unpinned npx or npm install commands, which can execute externally fetched package code. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Pin shadcn CLI versions in command examples and state that users must approve npm or npx execution before running them.

remediation.issue: Package installation guidance without version pinning
remediation.suggestion: Pin next-themes and related dependencies to known safe versions, and document that installs require network access.
Mark the Google Fonts import as optional and suggest self-hosting fonts for privacy-sensitive projects.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent React interfaces without rewriting common UI patterns. This skill provides shadcn/ui setup guidance, component examples, validation patterns, and theme references for Next.js projects.
actual_capabilities: Provides shadcn/ui initialization and component add guidance for Next.js projects.
Shows examples for buttons, forms, dialogs, alert dialogs, tables, cards, toasts, sidebars, and dark mode.
Demonstrates react-hook-form and Zod validation patterns for typed task forms.
Includes TanStack Table and sidebar navigation patterns for dashboard interfaces.
Supplies a TaskFlow theme reference with color tokens, typography, layout patterns, and globals.css guidance.
Documents a local verification step for checking required reference files.
limitations: It is focused on React and Next.js, not Vue, Svelte, Angular, or non-web interfaces.
Examples are templates and may need updates for newer shadcn/ui or dependency releases.
Installation commands require user approval in controlled or sandboxed environments.
The included TaskFlow theme is opinionated and may need adaptation for other brands.

use_cases.title: Start a Next.js UI Kit
use_cases.description: Use the setup and component guidance to add shadcn/ui foundations to a new app.

use_cases.title: Build Validated Product Forms
use_cases.description: Use the form examples to create accessible task forms with Zod validation and clear error states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Dashboard Components
use_cases.description: Use the table, sidebar, toast, and theme patterns to align dashboards around one component system.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Next.js project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a shadcn/ui setup plan for my Next.js app. Include the initial components I need for buttons, forms, dialogs, tables, and dark mode.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Validated Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a task form with shadcn/ui, react-hook-form, and Zod. Include field choices, validation rules, accessibility notes, and submit behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Dashboard
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced component migration for an existing app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my existing dashboard to use shadcn/ui cards, tables, toasts, sidebars, and dark mode. Keep the current routes and data model unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the TaskFlow Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an advanced TaskFlow interface using the included theme reference. Include component architecture, interaction states, responsive behavior, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Create a task creation flow for a Next.js dashboard.
output_examples.output: A component plan with a dialog trigger, validated task form, priority select, submit button states, and success or error toast behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing dashboard with shadcn/ui patterns.
output_examples.output: A refactor outline covering sidebar navigation, card summaries, data table columns, pagination behavior, and dark mode provider placement.

output_examples.input: Apply the TaskFlow visual style to my app.
output_examples.output: A theme application checklist with color roles, typography choices, layout background treatment, status indicators, and responsive spacing guidance.

best_practices: Confirm package installation commands before running them, especially npx commands that fetch current packages.
Use the included examples as patterns, then adapt labels, validation rules, and states to the product domain.
Pair the skill with current shadcn/ui documentation when dependency versions or component APIs may have changed.
anti_patterns: Do not apply the examples to non-React frameworks without rewriting the component model.
Do not copy the TaskFlow theme unchanged when brand, contrast, or accessibility requirements differ.
Do not run installation commands automatically in projects with strict dependency approval rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build accessible shadcn/ui interfaces for Next.js apps, including forms, dialogs, tables, sidebars, toasts, and dark mode.

faq.question: Does it install shadcn/ui automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance and examples. Users or agents should run installation commands only after approval.

faq.question: Is it limited to Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui project conventions.

faq.question: Does it cover form validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes react-hook-form and Zod patterns for typed fields, default values, validation messages, and submit handling.

faq.question: Can it help with dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes next-themes guidance, provider placement, a theme toggle pattern, and related component imports.

faq.question: Should I check current library documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. Use current shadcn/ui documentation when component APIs, package versions, or installation commands may have changed.
